title: Permutation in String
prompt: Given two strings `s1` and `s2`, return `true` if `s2` contains a permutation of `s1` as a contiguous substring, or `false` otherwise. In other words, check whether some substring of `s2` is an anagram of `s1`.

examples.explanation: "ba" is a substring of s2 and is a permutation of "ab".
No substring of s2 is a permutation of "ab".
s2 is shorter than s1, so no window of matching length even exists

constraints: s1 and s2 consist of lowercase English letters only
hints: A permutation of s1 is just any arrangement with the exact same character frequency counts as s1 — you don't need to generate permutations.
Use a fixed-size sliding window of length len(s1) over s2, and compare the window's character frequency count to s1's frequency count.

Instead of comparing full frequency maps at every position (which is slow), track a single 'matches' counter of how many of the 26 letters currently have equal counts in both windows, updating it incrementally as the window slides by one character at a time.

solution.approach: Build a frequency count of s1 and of the first window of s2 with the same length. Slide the window one character at a time: when adding the incoming character makes its count match s1's requirement, or removing the outgoing character makes its count match, increment a 'matches' counter; if either move breaks a previous match, decrement it. When matches reaches 26 (all letter counts equal), a permutation is present in the current window. This avoids recomparing full frequency maps at every shift.
